verdict.rationale: OpenClaw documents paired companion nodes (macOS/iOS/watchOS/Android/headless) that connect to the Gateway and expose camera, screen, device, and notification commands. The computer tool can also see and control a paired node's desktop, so the core of reaching beyond one machine is first-party. Media playback on paired devices is never documented, and there is no hands-on corroboration that the node camera, screen, or notification features work, so story coverage is incomplete. missing for 10: media playback on paired devices, depth of screenshot/camera/notification docs beyond summary lines, independent or hands-on corroboration of node features

support.subject: As a power user, the assistant reaches beyond one machine — paired phones and computers it can use for screenshots, camera, notifications, or media playback

citations.quote: A **node** is a companion device (macOS/iOS/watchOS/Android/headless) that connects to the Gateway with `role: "node"` and exposes a command surface (e.g. `camera.*`, `device.*`...)
Nodes: pairing, capabilities, permissions, and CLI helpers for camera/screen/device/notifications/system and the macOS widget panel
Computer use lets an agent see and control the Gateway's own desktop or a paired node's desktop through one built-in `computer` tool.
Pairing iOS/watchOS/Android nodes to a gateway
